{"sourceType":"ESA Tender Action","sourceSystem":"ESA esa-star Publication","sourcePage":"https://esastar-publication-ext.sso.esa.int/ESATenderActions/filter/open","id":195604,"idEra":25730,"activityNumber":"1000047540","contractNumber":"","tanumber":"1-13717","title":"MODULAR ROBUST WAVEFORM FOR END-TO-END COMMUNICATIONS - EXPRO+","description":"Objective: To develop a proof-of-concept of a modular robust waveform for E2E communications that offers further protection for the missions, in a modular approach in accordance with the mission security needs.Description:Intentional RF interference is a threat to space missions, as it can disrupt the radio links between satellite and ground/users. There are waveform techniques that can counter or mitigate the impact of that interference but they need to be designed specifically against reference threats. This activity is aimed at developing a modular robust waveform for end-to-end (E2E) communications offering further protection for the missions, by designing the waveform aspects as well as the receiver operations. It will consider typical RF threats and tune the waveform against the most common ones, so that space missions do not have to develop new solutions for their case. The design of the modular robust waveform can include cryptographically robust spread sequences that can be used to drive a frequency hopping scheme, or a direct Sequence spread spectrum modulation, coupled with Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM). The adaptation algorithm of the ACM can cover both the typical Modulation and Coding schemes as well as the Transmission Security (TRANSEC) functions (e.g. Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum and Frequency Hopping), providing flexible level of protection based on the link conditions.
